title: Sashi Cheliah, MasterChef Australia Winner, to Judge Celebrity MasterChef Tamil
excerpt: The 2018 MasterChef Australia champion joins the judging panel of the Samantha Ruth Prabhu-hosted celebrity spin-off, a launch title for Sony Pictures Networks India's new Tamil channel, Sony VIZHA.
body:
• Sashi Cheliah, the winner of MasterChef Australia Season 10, will take a seat on the judging panel of Celebrity MasterChef Tamil, according to NDTV and Telugu Times.
  • The celebrity edition, hosted by actor Samantha Ruth Prabhu, will air on Sony Pictures Networks India's new premium Tamil channel, Sony VIZHA, and stream on SonyLIV.
  • Cheliah is Singaporean-born with Coimbatore-origin family roots, and the role marks a high-profile return to his Tamil heritage — he built his reputation on the Australian show on bold, unapologetic flavour.
  • The show is expected to premiere in late 2026; the rest of the judging panel and the celebrity contestant lineup have not yet been announced.

A global MasterChef takes the Tamil hot seat

Sashi Cheliah, the chef who went from Singapore's elite police tactical unit to the top of the MasterChef Australia kitchen, is joining Celebrity MasterChef Tamil as a judge. The casting, reported this week by NDTV and Telugu Times, places the 2018 MasterChef Australia champion on the judging panel of Sony Pictures Networks India's new celebrity spin-off of the global cooking format.

The show will be hosted by actor Samantha Ruth Prabhu and is a flagship launch for Sony VIZHA, SPNI's new premium Tamil entertainment channel, with episodes also streaming on SonyLIV. Banijay Asia is producing the series, which brings the MasterChef format to Tamil audiences with an all-celebrity contestant lineup — Tamil entertainment personalities trading film sets for cooking stations.

Context & background

Sony Pictures Networks India unveiled Celebrity MasterChef Tamil on August 15, 2026, with Samantha Ruth Prabhu as host. Sony describes Sony VIZHA as "a premium Tamil entertainment brand that celebrates Tamil culture and is crafted for a global audience," and the celebrity cooking show is positioned as one of its key launch offerings.

Cheliah's appointment lands eight years after his 2018 victory on MasterChef Australia, where the judges named him the season's "king of flavours." He won the title with a fish curry and sambal prawns with cumin rice — dedicated to his aunt — that earned a perfect score in the finale against runner-up Ben Borsht.

His ties to Tamil television are not new: he has appeared on MasterChef India Tamil, headlining the Season 2 immunity pin challenge, and he runs Pandan Club at T Nagar in Chennai, serving Peranakan cuisine, which he told Mint was the first of its kind in India.

Impact & analysis

Casting Cheliah is a credibility play. Celebrity cooking shows live or die on the authority of the judging panel, and a MasterChef winner who built his brand on flavour-first cooking gives the format weight with Tamil audiences — while his international profile gives Sony VIZHA a name that travels beyond the Tamil market.

"We don't believe in being conservative in the kitchen!"

— Sashi Cheliah, in an interview with Global Indian, on his family's approach to flavour

The choice also signals how the Tamil show intends to differentiate itself. Regular celebrity editions in Hindi have leaned on star judges; bringing in a winner from a foreign edition — rather than a television personality — suggests the producers want the food judged on technique, not just celebrity theatre.

For Sony VIZHA, the stakes are launch-season stakes: new channels live on tentpole programming, and a celebrity edition fronted by Prabhu and judged by an international winner is the channel's clearest bid for a first-season conversation-starter.

A diaspora homecoming

Cheliah's story is a diaspora arc in the truest sense. Born and raised in Singapore to a family of Coimbatore origin, he served as a commando in the Singapore armed forces before 13 years in the police's elite Special Tactics and Rescue (STAR) unit. He moved to Adelaide for work-life balance, auditioned for MasterChef Australia in 2018, and won — becoming the show's first winner of Indian descent. He now runs Gaja by Sashi in Adelaide.

"Food has a wonderful way of bringing people together, creating memories, and revealing a side of you that the cameras don't usually get to see."

— Samantha Ruth Prabhu, host of Celebrity MasterChef Tamil, in a statement released by Sony Pictures Networks India

That a chef formed across Singapore, Adelaide and Chennai will judge Tamil celebrities on their cooking is a neat full circle: talent formed abroad returning to the culture's home turf on its biggest stages.

What's next

The show is expected to premiere in late 2026 on Sony VIZHA and SonyLIV, though Sony has not yet announced an exact date. The remaining judges and the celebrity contestant roster are still under wraps — the August promo teased that Prabhu herself would not reveal who is cooking. Expect casting announcements to roll out as the channel's launch programming firms up in the coming weeks.

nri_angle: Sashi Cheliah — Singaporean-born, of Coimbatore-origin family, based in Adelaide — brings the diaspora's culinary success story full circle by judging Tamil celebrities on Sony VIZHA.
